findings.quote: represent は「完全に同じ」という意味ではなく、記号や形が何かを示すこと。
findings.reason: This excludes an established meaning already instantiated by the decision/major-change example: an event can itself constitute a change, risk or opportunity. The common proportion use, in which members or an amount constitute part of a total, is also not taught by the dot/symbol example.
findings.minimal_action: Explicitly distinguish actual constitution/equivalence or a share of a whole from symbolic representation. Supply suitable frames, definition and a proportion example; retain and place the existing major-change example accurately. Do not retain the categorical identity exclusion.

findings.quote: 記号・数字・色・行為・作品などが、何かの意味や概念を示すこと。
findings.reason: Depicting a scene/person and presenting somebody as having a quality are important meanings not adequately explained by symbolism or by data as a graph. The object-as construction can describe an unfair portrayal or claim. Reflexive represent oneself as is especially liable to confusion with acting as one’s own agent.
findings.minimal_action: Provide explicit depiction/characterization coverage with complete represent someone/something and represent someone/something as + noun/adjective/being frames, natural matched examples and an accuracy qualification. Include the useful represent oneself as variant; distinguish it from representing oneself in a legal or agency context. Keep visual depiction and character-description distinctions clear even if they share one coherent block.

findings.quote: ・underrepresented（形容詞）— 十分に代表されていない。
findings.reason: The passive be represented can mean being present or included to a degree in a group, place or dataset, without an agent acting on somebody’s behalf. The derived adjective mention does not teach that construction.
findings.minimal_action: Add a clearly distinguished be (well/poorly/equally) represented in/on frame and matched example. Explain the inclusion/proportion meaning and distinguish an agentive by-phrase. Clarify underrepresented’s numerical/presence application where useful without inventing a separate adjective definition for every passive.

findings.quote: The two numbered blocks cover only agency and symbolic meaning.
findings.reason: Formal represent something to somebody and represent (to somebody) that-clause report a statement, concern or protest. Neither current block teaches those complement roles or the statement’s lack of a truth guarantee.
findings.minimal_action: Add concise, explicitly formal coverage with complete recipient/content frames and one or more matched examples sufficient to distinguish noun-content from a that-clause. Do not invent legal procedural guarantees or claim that all such statements are true.

findings.quote: 表す、象徴する、意味する。
findings.reason: Being a specimen or typical example is not the same relation as a sign conventionally standing for something. Multiple dictionaries record the former, but there is no explanation or matching example here.
findings.minimal_action: Add a concise typifying/embodying or specimen note and matched example within a coherent appropriate sense, or a separate block if needed for accurate boundaries. A separate numbered block for every source’s division is not required.

findings.reason: The selected example and the explanatory distinction illustrate symbolic meaning, not acting or speaking as a person’s agent. The stand-for definition also combines support with symbolism without selecting an example-compatible comparison sense.
findings.minimal_action: Move the complete flag example/comparison to the symbolism sense, selecting its symbolic definition and preserving the example. Do not claim stand for can never have other represent/support meanings.

findings.quote: represent が正しく立場や事実を示すのに対し、misrepresent は不正確に伝える。
findings.reason: Represent does not by itself guarantee accurate portrayal or truthful assertion. Misrepresent’s selected account-distortion meaning is also not the opposite of serving as an agent; this entry’s own article/views example belongs to portrayal or reporting.
findings.minimal_action: Remove the automatic correctness claim and retain the useful full misrepresent block as an explicit accuracy contrast near depiction/description. Explain that accurate representation contrasts with misrepresentation; plain represent is not a truth certificate.

findings.reason: As currently attached to agency and symbolism, these selected examples do not establish clear opposites on the same lexical axis. Excluding a business differs from speaking for it; hiding facts or making wording unclear differs from a symbol standing for an idea. Useful contrasts need not be presented as lexical antonyms.
findings.minimal_action: Preserve these useful definitions/scores/examples in explicitly labelled contextual contrast notes unless the revised entry supplies a genuine same-axis selected sense. If exclude is used with an inclusion/presence reading, define the actual inclusion/exclusion relation and compatible roles. Do not invent antonyms to fill a quota.

findings.quote: represent a change/increase/risk / represent data as + 名詞 / represent + percentage/number
findings.reason: The first compressed alternatives produce a increase. The graph example is passive results-as-graph whereas its heading is active data-as-format. The dot example has a symbol as subject and ten people as the represented quantity, while its use gloss says a number explains what it shows. Legacy + and naked placeholder notation also obscures complete frames; the agentive passive is absent from the main grammar overview.
findings.minimal_action: Use full article-safe alternatives, e.g. represent a change / represent an increase / represent a risk. Match the graph heading to the passive example, and distinguish symbolic quantity representation from constituting a percentage. Correct subject-role wording for Each dot represents ten people. Include the existing agentive passive in sense 1 grammar and normalize placeholders without changing natural original sentences.

findings.quote: 【語法・注意】represent は「完全に同じ」という意味ではなく…
findings.reason: The entry lacks the useful contrast between normally stative symbolism/constitution and ongoing agency or depiction. A blanket no-progressive rule would be wrong, but no distinction is currently given.
findings.minimal_action: Add a short sense-limited note: symbolic/equivalent readings are normally not progressive, while an ongoing act of representing someone can be progressive. Avoid transferring no-passive/no-progressive labels from one source sense to every use of represent.

findings.quote: その会社は現地代理店に代表されている。
findings.reason: The passive calque is unnatural for ordinary business agency. Local agent need not specifically be a retail agency; the point is acting for the company.
findings.minimal_action: Use a natural agency translation such as 現地の代理人がその会社の代理を務めている。 Preserve the English sentence. In the court example, 法廷で彼の弁護を担当した is also a clear natural rendering, without adding procedural claims.

findings.quote: ＃意味や関連情報の出力（日本語訳） / 【頻度】〈頻度: 8/10〉 / 共通コアは…
findings.reason: The legacy heading, frequency notation, equal UK/US duplication and missing required trailing spaces need current body-format normalization. The common-core explanation is embedded in etymology and names depiction despite missing substantive depiction coverage.
findings.minimal_action: Apply the supported current v5 body heading/spacing/notation while preserving original generation prompt_version metadata. After meaningful senses are corrected, reassess core eligibility and write a real 1–2 sentence shared kernel with exact sense-title branches if the resulting article meets the rule. Do not use a forced core to hide differences between agency, portrayal, symbolic reference and actual constitution.

findings.reason: The etymological gloss is supportable, but learners may infer that ordinary represent also means simply present again with the same pronunciation. Original dictionaries separately record re-present with /riː/ and a repeated-presentation meaning.
findings.minimal_action: A short spelling/pronunciation distinction in pronunciation, etymology or usage would be useful: re-present means 再び提示・提出する and begins with /ˌriː/. Do not require a large new sense block or merge the forms indiscriminately.

No demonstrated global-English ordinal band contradiction in the selected existing scores. Sense 2 is currently conflated; assess any new separated senses editorially rather than recycling a whole-word frequency or inventing corpus counts.

Public defender is not defined in English by popular election, but 公選弁護人 is an attested Japanese translation variant in first-party indexed material. 公設弁護人 or a brief publicly funded defender gloss can improve clarity. The legal examples make only ordinary lexical claims; no legal-procedure expansion is needed.
Presence (存在、出席), present and representative are genuine related family items. Additional obscure relatives are not needed.
